title: 2007 AMC 12A Problem 15
statement: The set \(\{3,6,9,10\}\) is augmented by a fifth element \(n,\) not equal to any of the other four. The median of the resulting set is equal to its mean. What is the sum of all possible values of \(n?\)

solutions.text:
The mean is \(\dfrac{28+n}{5}.\)

If \(n\lt 6,\) the median is \(6,\) so \(28+n=30\) and \(n=2.\)

If \(6\lt n\lt 9,\) the median is \(n,\) so \(28+n=5n\) and \(n=7.\)

If \(n\gt 9,\) the median is \(9,\) so \(28+n=45\) and \(n=17.\)

The sum of all possible values is \(2+7+17=26.\)

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: The mean of the five numbers is \(\dfrac{28+n}{5}\)
Split into cases: the median is \(6\) when \(n\lt 6,\) it is \(n\) when \(6\lt n\lt 9,\) and \(9\) when \(n\gt 9\)
